note: Cross-language storage-binding corpus for kit/storage/kv on the SQLite backend. Every SDK that implements the kv contract MUST be able to write this corpus to a SQLite file and read back every key, with the exact value bytes, from a store opened by any other SDK against that same file. The `kv.key` column is TEXT in every implementation: SQLite compares storage class before value, so a BLOB-bound key never equals a TEXT-bound one and cross-language reads would silently miss. Keys and values are hex so JSON carries non-UTF-8 bytes losslessly. `list_order` is the full corpus under `ORDER BY key`, i.e. SQLite's default BINARY collation, which is memcmp over the stored bytes and therefore identical to Go's string ordering — prefix scans depend on that equivalence holding under TEXT. The list/List operation itself issues no ORDER BY, so its row order is unspecified: compare its result as a set, and assert `list_order` only against an explicitly ordered query. `expect_hex` in `prefix_scans` is likewise given in collation order and compared as a set.

cases.name: empty-value
cases.note: "empty" -> zero-length value. Must round-trip as present-but-empty, not absent.

cases.name: trailing-ff
cases.note: "data\xff" -> "trailing". Not valid UTF-8; the prefix that broke prefixEnd.

cases.name: outside-ff-prefix
cases.note: "dataf" -> "outside". Sorts near the 0xff keys but is outside the prefix range; guards an over-wide upper bound.

cases.name: all-ff-double
cases.note: "\xff\xff" -> "allff". Prefix with no successor: the scan must be lower-bounded only.

cases.name: all-ff-child
cases.note: "\xff\xffz" -> "allffz". Must be reachable from the all-0xff prefix.

cases.name: high-byte-run
cases.note: "\xfe\xfd\xfc" -> "high". Non-UTF-8 bytes that are not 0xff; guards a fix that special-cases 0xff only.

cases.name: leading-nul
cases.note: "\x00lead" -> "nullead". Leading NUL must not truncate the key; sqlite3_bind_text64 is length-counted, C-string semantics would drop this to the empty key.

cases.name: embedded-nul
cases.note: "emb\x00ed" -> "embnul". Interior NUL must survive the round trip and stay distinct from "emb".

cases.name: value-with-nul-and-ff
cases.note: "binval" -> "\x00\xff\x00\xff". The value column is BLOB; binary values must survive unchanged.

cases.name: utf8-multibyte
cases.note: "l\u2713" -> "\u2713". Valid multi-byte UTF-8, to prove the TEXT binding is not mangling well-formed text.

cases.name: invalid-utf8-continuation
cases.note: "l\x80" -> "bad2". A bare continuation byte: invalid UTF-8 that a String-typed API could not represent at all.

prefix_scans.name: empty-prefix-lists-all
prefix_scans.note: Empty prefix is unbounded: every live key, in BINARY collation order.

prefix_scans.name: trailing-ff-prefix
prefix_scans.note: prefixEnd("data\xff") drops the 0xff and increments, giving "datb"; "dataf" must stay out.

prefix_scans.name: all-ff-prefix-unbounded
prefix_scans.note: All-0xff prefix has no successor, so the scan is lower-bounded only and must still exclude everything below it.

prefix_scans.name: nul-prefix-is-not-empty-prefix
prefix_scans.note: A 0x00 prefix is a real one-byte prefix, not the empty/unbounded case.

prefix_scans.name: emb-prefix-stops-at-nul
prefix_scans.note: "emb" must match the embedded-NUL key; a C-string truncation bug would make these two keys collide instead.
